newsitem.title: USA: U.S. FERC backs gas transport rate settlement.
newsitem.headline: U.S. FERC backs gas transport rate settlement.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission on Wednesday approved a long-contested rate settlement on a pipeline expansion built by Pacific Gas Transmission Co, a unit of Pacific Gas and Electric.

The pipeline's original customers had first balked at the company's plan to roll in the costs of the expansion into the rates of all of its existing and new customers, instead of charging higher rates only to new users.
"The problem was the mismatch in the rate base," said PGT spokesman David Dodson. "We were trying to roll-in on a small rate base," which had basically consisted of three customers.

The expansion from northern Idaho to the California-Wyoming border went on line in November 1993, adding 960,000 million Btu's of capacity at a cost of $852 million, with annual operating costs of $206 million.

Most customers and the California Public Utility Commission eventually backed the settlement which rolled the expansion costs into the whole system for a rate of 26.3 cents per MMBtu, with discounts for certain users for six years.
The settlement provided an 8.5 cent discount to local distribution companies which acquired capacity held by Northwest Pipeline Corp, a unit of Williams Cos Inc.
It gave a 6.4 cent discount to captive residential and small commercial natural gas users, and a 2.0 cent discount to customers which acquired some of PG&E's capacity.
PGT's competitor El Paso Natural Gas Co, and shippers Sierra Pacific Resources and Portland General Electric Co, among others, opposed the settlement.
But Commissioner Donald Santa said the shippers should be happy with the rate they got, warning that had the case been litigated, "they would have ended up worse off."
